projects.title: Lead Routing Reliability Demo
projects.summary: A lead-intake and routing workflow built to survive the boring failures that break real automations: duplicates, partial failures, retries and replay.
bullets: Safe replay without duplicate side effects
projects.one_liner: Lead intake that survives duplicate deliveries, a transient API failure and a failed run being safely replayed.
projects.problem: Lead workflows break on the boring parts: the same webhook fires twice, an API returns 503 mid-run, and the retry creates a second lead. Most demos only show the happy path.
projects.build: An n8n lead-intake and routing workflow where every webhook receipt is idempotent (duplicate deliveries collapse to one record), validation gates entry, retries use backoff with explicit failure paths, and a safe replay recovers failed runs without duplicating side effects. Every decision is logged for audit.
reliability: Idempotency keys on intake — duplicate webhooks collapse to a single record
Retries with backoff and explicit failure paths — no silent loops
Safe replay: failed runs re-execute without double-processing
Failure alerts instead of silent breakage
Audit trail of every route decision
projects.proof: 23/23 acceptance tests in the repo's evidence/acceptance-summary.json — covering duplicate delivery, transient failure, replay and routing edge cases. Demo uses synthetic data.
projects.link_note: The recording is a screen capture of the workflow running in n8n — recorded, not live.

video.caption: Recorded walkthrough of the workflow running in n8n. Burned-in captions, no voice-over required.

observable: A valid lead arrives and is routed, with the route decision recorded
The same delivery arriving twice produces one intended action, not two
A simulated transient failure is retried on the failure path instead of silently dying
A failed run can be replayed without repeating its side effects
projects.tested: 23 acceptance checks were run locally against the workflow (n8n 1.121.3): input validation and rejection, idempotency and duplicate handling, concurrency and atomic claim, retry orchestration with backoff, transient/429/503 classification, partial-failure handling, replay without repeated side effects, and completion receipts with audit logging. All 23 passed.
projects.not_tested: Not a production deployment and no real client traffic. Not tested at multi-tenant scale, against live third-party APIs, or for universal recovery from every possible failure mode. The 23 checks cover the scenarios listed in the repo's acceptance summary, not an open-ended guarantee.
evidence: Architecture preflight: main, retry subworkflow, replay and monitor workflows all active and callable
No disabled critical nodes; no code-node network or retry loops
Failure, retry and replay paths are separated into their own workflows

projects.title: AI Lead Classifier
projects.summary: A real LLM call inside n8n using Hive / GLM 5.3 Flash. The workflow trusts nothing blindly: output is parsed, schema-validated, routed and rejected cleanly when the model misbehaves.
bullets: Malformed output returns an error, not a guess
projects.one_liner: A real LLM call inside n8n that validates structured output, retries transient failures, and refuses to guess when the model misbehaves.
projects.problem: LLM integrations fail quietly: the model returns malformed JSON, the API returns 503, or the output drifts outside the schema — and the workflow routes whatever it got anyway.
projects.build: An n8n workflow making a real Hive API call to GLM 5.3 Flash for lead classification (category, urgency, intent). The response is parsed and schema-validated before routing; transient failures retry with backoff; malformed or invalid output returns a clean rejection — never a guess. Forced-failure tests prove each path.
reliability: Schema validation before any routing decision
Malformed output → explicit error, not a fabricated result
Forced-failure test path proves the failure branch works
Structured JSON output consumed downstream without re-parsing
projects.proof: 9/9 test cases passed (test_cases.json, retry-evidence.json, results.json in repo). Real screenshots: workflow canvas + successful execution. Demo uses synthetic data.

media.alt: n8n workflow canvas of the AI lead classifier
media.caption: Workflow canvas — real n8n screenshot

observable: A real API call returns a structured classification (category, urgency, intent, confidence)
Output that fails schema validation is rejected with an explicit error instead of a guess
A simulated 503 triggers retry handling, and a recovered retry is captured as evidence
Missing input is rejected at validation before any model call is made
projects.tested: 9 acceptance cases were run against the live n8n webhook, using a real Hive API call (GLM 5.3 Flash). Coverage: happy-path classifications, missing input, malformed JSON from the model, forced 503 through all retries, schema-invalid values, and a transient 503 that recovered on retry. All 9 passed.
projects.not_tested: A schema-valid response is not proof of classification accuracy — these are synthetic test messages, not labelled real-world data, so no accuracy rate is claimed. Not tested under production volume, rate limits or provider outages. No business outcome, time saving or revenue is measured.
evidence: 9/9 cases passed — results.json with per-case expected vs actual
Forced-failure path observed 3 attempts (1 initial + 2 retries) with backoff, then a clean failure
Transient 503 recovered on the second attempt against the real API
Malformed output returns 502, never a fabricated classification

projects.title: Opportunity Engine
projects.summary: A private internal tool: it collects leads from multiple sources, scores them, drafts outreach and tracks replies — and sends nothing without an explicit human approval step.
projects.one_liner: A private internal engineering tool, shown here only as a secondary example: it is not client work and is not evidence of client acquisition results.
projects.problem: Solo operators lose track of lead sources and follow-ups, but fully automated outreach is not acceptable either.
projects.disclosure: Private internal tool • not client work
projects.tested: A regression suite covering approval binding and send safety was run after a repair of this system: 33 checks, all passing.
projects.not_tested: Not production-verified end to end. Live Gmail polling was not exercised after the change, the search layer was not covered by the cursor tests, and one requirement-matching check remains vocabulary-driven and needs manual review. No client results, revenue or conversion figures are claimed.
evidence: Approval is bound to exact content: editing a draft or changing the recipient invalidates it
A message queue holds nothing that could send without an approval matching its current content
Duplicate handling and watermark rules covered by regression checks
projects.link_note: No repository, screenshots, URLs or operational data are published for this internal tool.
